PROJECT.WHAT: Agent1st — behavior-layer protocol for AI-agent software development
PROJECT.WHY: Reduce drift between human intent and agent execution across long-lived projects

USECASE_ADOPT.WHAT: Drop AGENTS.md into a project; agent reads it and operates accordingly
USECASE_ADOPT.WHY: Adoption friction is the main barrier; minimal AGENTS.md must stay drop-in

USECASE_EXTEND.WHAT: Long-lived project adds the WHY layer on top of minimal AGENTS.md
USECASE_EXTEND.WHY: Drift across sessions kills real projects; WHY layer makes intent durable

USECASE_CONTRIBUTE.WHAT: Agent proposes a change to the protocol itself
USECASE_CONTRIBUTE.WHY: Protocol is agent-developed; contribution path must be legible to agents

USECASE_HANDOFF.WHAT: Work transfers between agents across sessions without repeating discoveries
USECASE_HANDOFF.WHY: Compaction and session ends lose context; a durable transfer artifact is the only thing that survives

USECASE_REVIEW.WHAT: A human or agent audits whether a completion claim matches evidence
USECASE_REVIEW.WHY: Completion without proof is storytelling; the repo must make the audit possible

FEATURE_CORE.INTENT: Minimal AGENTS.md — 6 distinct principles, 118 lines, delta-layer, drop-in

ACCEPT.CHECK: Every principle has WHY and IF MISSING blocks
No line contradicts what a current harness enforces (DESIGN.md §2a)
File stays under 200 lines without merging distinct concepts for mechanical compression
Contains principles, not release notes or compatibility routing

FEATURE_WHY.INTENT: Why1st (the WHY layer) — PRD + Why Graph + Contracts + Validator MVP, one proven shape

ACCEPT.CHECK: Why1st.md explains the idea before any template is shown
Each paired file is usable standalone and coherent together
At least one dogfooded example lives in this repo
A public runnable source example checks anchors and behavior separately
A deterministic validator runs over the dogfooded graph and exits 0

FEATURE_BRIDGE.INTENT: Claude Code bridge — CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md, no second source of truth

FEATURE_DESIGN.INTENT: Design rationale for agents modifying the protocol

FEATURE_EVOLVE.INTENT: Evolution history — what changed, what was rejected, and why

FEATURE_FOUND.INTENT: Research foundations with honest evidence labels, counter-arguments, and a model-shift register

FEATURE_ROAD.INTENT: Roadmap with proposed / held / rejected items; every held item carries a probe or a date

FEATURE_HANDOFF.INTENT: Handoff briefs as first-class artifacts: one template, three modes, evidence over claims
